spec.name: Workflow agent assignments and validator cohorts

payload.body: Graph workflows configure their agents as bare runtime triples: the implementer is backend/model/effort with no behavioral identity, and every execution context is reviewed by exactly one generic validator with no specialist focus. Roadmap D3 calls for multiple named specialist validators per context (security, type safety, test quality) and configurable implementer personas — most of the Adversarial Verification pattern in first-class form. The agent-profile-library spec delivers the shared profile library and conversation consumer; this spec delivers the workflow consumers: implementer assignments drawn from the library, and specialist validator cohorts with deterministic all-of semantics, per-assignment lane identity, mechanically read-only review, and transport-level prompt authority.
payload.title: Problem

payload.body: Workflow configuration selects agents as assignments from the shared profile library: one implementer assignment per context, and an ordered cohort of specialist validator assignments with stable use-site identity. A cohort reviews one frozen candidate deterministically — all required validators must pass the same candidate, the cohort charges one validation iteration per semantic round regardless of validator count, findings stay grouped by assignment, and infrastructure failures never masquerade as review verdicts. Validators become mechanically read-only. Prompt authority is enforced at the transport level for task-strategy validation, with the role contract dominant over user-authored profile text. Existing persisted configuration migrates once, with hard cutover.
payload.title: Outcomes

payload.body: Multiple implementers editing one context (multi-implementer coordination overlaps later roadmap work; one implementer per context stands). Advisory non-gating validators (required-only in v1; advisory is a later explicit mode if evidence demands it). Migrating the D1 plan-repair agent onto the library (future consumer; its evidence integration here is read-only). Any inbound compatibility parser for legacy singleton config shapes (locked: hard cutover). Agent-planned lane assignment and same-worktree parallelism (roadmap D5). New mutation paths outside the existing live-edit choke point. Field-merging profiles across cascade tiers — assignments replace as whole units.
payload.title: Non-goals

payload.body: Locked by Alex 2026-08-01 via the ticket #39 collaboration, as amended by Alex 2026-08-03 during requirements review: (1) one-time migration of persisted implementer/validator config onto built-in profile assignments, hard cutover, no inbound compatibility parser; the archived-execution-blob read-path decode floor is APPROVED (Alex 2026-08-03) as the single recorded backward-compatibility exception — archived blobs keep a read-only legacy decoder and are never rewritten; (2) cutover requires terminal executions: the migration auto-aborts any non-terminal execution with a distinct migration-cutover abort reason surfaced in the inspector, and no live runtime state (working definitions, lane keys, continuity, pending questions) is migrated (Alex 2026-08-03); (3) assignments are replaced whole at cascade boundaries (global -> workflow -> context), never field-merged; (4) a semantic cohort failure charges exactly one validation iteration and one consecutive-failure count; (5) validators are mechanically read-only via a backend-enforced write-restriction envelope with an explicit per-lane write allowlist — this supersedes the 2026-08-01 detect-restore-and-bound mutation handling, which is dropped along with mutation incidents, bounds, and the mutation halt kind (Alex 2026-08-03); (6) profile text enters task-strategy validation through executeWorkflowTaskRun.systemInstructions via the companion spec's composer, extended here with the single focus-aware interface, role contract dominant, with adversarial-profile and adversarial-focus tests on both backends; (7) the seeded default remains a single general-reviewer assignment so existing workflows keep one reviewer invocation per round; (8) dynamic mutation rides the doc 05/06 live-edit surface (pause-to-edit for started contexts) — no new choke points; (9) validator questions are per-lane: multiple validators in one context may park questions simultaneously, surfaced together in Needs You, and a lane awaiting an answer is an unsettled round outcome — this supersedes the per-context question mutex (Alex 2026-08-03); (10) cohort parallelism is subordinate to the engine's existing global query budget (Alex 2026-08-03). Implementation prerequisite: this spec's implementation does not start until the agent-profile-library spec's library service, snapshot contract (including renderedInstructionBlock), and composer are merged — the governing charter and roadmap D3 wording must be amended to record this dependency (D3 is two sequenced specs, no longer 'independent of everything else'). Engineering contract per AGENTS.md: workflow modules per the adoption matrix, publication seam for events, round-trip contract tests for persisted shapes, full repository suite green at the published tip before closeout.
payload.title: Constraints (locked decisions)

payload.body: A real execution context gated by at least two specialist validators produces independent verdicts against the same frozen candidate (live proof at the delivery gate). Existing workflows run unchanged after migration: one reviewer invocation per validation round and unchanged iteration/circuit-breaker accounting (the non-empty rendered profile block necessarily adds prompt tokens, so cost parity is measured in invocations and accounting, not tokens). A cohort failure consumes one iteration regardless of validator count. An adversarial profile cannot expand scope, edit the candidate, bypass acceptance criteria, or replace the verdict schema on either backend.
payload.title: Success measures

payload.body: Full design and negotiation record: memory-bank/collaboration/559ea789-4903-4075-a1b7-a2df1d2675c1/round-1/agent_one/final_answer/answer.md and audit.md on branch csm/ticket-workflow-vision-roadmap-d0-d2-delivered-pick-up-at-d3-d4-e65782. Current config surfaces: src/lib/workflow-graph/resolve-config.ts (SEEDED_WORKFLOW_DEFAULTS, cascade), src/lib/workflow-graph/config-schemas.ts (per-backend agent union; validator union whose type field is the execution strategy, independent of backend, with per-validator enabled and continuity). Task-strategy instruction transport: executeWorkflowTaskRun.systemInstructions. Live-edit lifecycle: started contexts require pause-to-edit (runtime-edits.ts) and pausing aborts validator lanes (workflow-manager.ts) — R11 aligns with that locked D0 lifecycle rather than inventing staged edits. Read-only enforcement surfaces: Codex task runs already accept per-run sandboxMode (src/lib/agent-backends/codex/task-runner.ts); the Claude task runner currently drops sandbox fields and runs with bypassed permissions (src/lib/agent-backends/claude/task-runner.ts), while the installed Claude Agent SDK supports OS-level command sandboxing (sandbox enabled/failIfUnavailable/allowUnsandboxedCommands:false with a filesystem write allowlist) plus permission rules for the file-mutation tools — the envelope is wiring at the backend-neutral capability seam, not new backend capability. Companion spec: agent-profile-library (library domain, resolver, snapshot contract incl. renderedInstructionBlock, neutral composer — prerequisites consumed here). NOTE for the governing records: this dependency means roadmap D3's 'independent of everything else' phrasing and the ticket charter's equivalent line are stale — D3 is now two sequenced specs, the second dependent on the first; the alignment charter should be amended accordingly at the next human touchpoint. Roadmap: docs/roadmap.md D3.
payload.title: Context and references

payload.statement: Workflow configuration shall adopt AgentAssignment { id (stable use-site identity), profile (qualified AgentProfileRef), focus (optional free text), agent (the existing per-backend discriminated runtime union, concrete) }. Validator cohort entries additionally carry the fields today's singleton validator owns: execution strategy (conversation-strategy or task-strategy, independent of backend exactly as the current type field is) and a per-assignment continuity policy, with no silent loss of any currently expressible configuration — legacy shapes whose optional fields are omitted (e.g. Codex validator model/effort) migrate by materializing the effective values the existing resolver computes today, written concretely into the assignment. The implementer at every cascade level shall become an AgentAssignment, and cascade resolution (global -> workflow -> context) shall replace the whole assignment at each override boundary — never merge fields across tiers.

payload.text: Cascade tests prove whole-assignment replacement (profile, focus, strategy, continuity, and runtime together) with no cross-tier field mixing, across both execution strategies and both backends including strategy/backend combinations legal today (e.g. a Codex agent under conversation strategy); per-assignment continuity policy and disabled-state retention round-trip through persistence; runtime typing reuses the per-backend union so an invalid backend/model pairing is refused.

payload.statement: contextValidator configuration shall become an ordered validator cohort with whole-set semantics per cascade tier: absent inherits, use replaces the entire set, and disabled turns agent validation off while preserving the dormant assignments (their profiles, strategy, continuity, and runtime) so re-enabling restores them without loss. A use set shall contain at least one assignment — an empty use is refused at parse/validate so all-of validation can never vacuously pass. Assignment ids follow a normalized bounded grammar (lowercase kebab-case, 1-64 chars, unique within the context); the same profile may appear in multiple entries with different focus. The seeded default shall remain exactly one general-reviewer assignment, single-sourced in SEEDED_WORKFLOW_DEFAULTS, preserving the current cost profile.

payload.text: Tests cover inherit/use/disabled at each cascade tier; an empty use set is refused with a located error; assignment ids violating the grammar (uppercase, overlong, invalid characters) or duplicated within a context are refused; the same profile appears twice with different focus successfully; the seeded default resolves to one general-reviewer assignment.

payload.statement: A one-time migration shall convert every persisted holder of the legacy shapes with an explicit per-surface migration table: global config workflowDefaults (config.json), global- and project-scope workflow definition documents in scoped storage, and the schema floor for execution rows. Cutover requires cutover-terminal executions, with the status taxonomy enumerated explicitly: an execution is cutover-terminal only when it has finished with no remaining resume path (completed, or aborted/failed with no resume); every other status — running, paused, pending, and halted-but-resumable alike — is aborted by the migration with a distinct migration-cutover abort reason surfaced in the inspector, ending its resume path, and no live runtime state (working definitions, validator lane keys, continuity records, pending questions) is migrated. Mapping rules: implementer runtime triples become assignments (id: implementer) on builtin:general-implementer preserving backend/model/effort; the singleton contextValidator becomes a cohort of one assignment (id: general) on builtin:general-reviewer preserving its execution strategy (type), continuity policy, and runtime — omitted optional fields (e.g. Codex model/effort) materialize to the effective values the current resolver computes; enabled:false migrates to a disabled cohort that carries the dormant assignment. Archived execution blobs — including executions aborted at cutover — are historical records with an approved read-path decode floor, the single recorded backward-compatibility exception (Alex 2026-08-03); they are never rewritten. The migration shall be idempotent and crash-recoverable (resumable without double-applying), with failure-injection tests. After cutover, legacy shapes at parse/validate are refused with a located error naming the expected assignment form; no inbound compatibility parser shall exist outside the archived-blob decode floor.

payload.text: Migration tests load pre-migration fixtures for every inventory surface — config.json workflowDefaults and global and project definition documents — and prove the migrated forms preserve strategy, enabled state, continuity, and runtime exactly (including enabled:false to disabled cohort and omitted optional Codex fields materialized to the resolver's effective values); a fixture with a running execution proves cutover aborts it with the migration-cutover abort reason and its archived record still decodes read-only; a fixture with a halted-but-resumable execution proves cutover aborts it and its resume path is refused post-cutover; a terminal execution's archived blob decodes unchanged; re-running the migration is a no-op; a simulated crash mid-migration recovers without double-applying; the migration is registered in the runner with floor behavior per the migrations contract.

Post-cutover, a legacy singleton validator/implementer shape submitted through definition authoring or workflow validate is refused with a located error naming the use site and expected form; no code path silently normalizes it.

payload.statement: Execution start shall resolve every assignment's profile reference into the workingDefinition as the companion spec's full resolved snapshot — { tier, id, name, revision, sourceContentHash, instructions, renderedInstructionBlock, resolvedInstructionHash } — rendered through the one focus-aware composer interface this spec adds to the companion domain (an optional assignment-focus input on the same composer): focus is normalized and size-capped, subject to the same delimiter/fence refusal rules as profile content, rendered exactly once inside the block (never delivered through a second channel), and covered by resolvedInstructionHash. Workflow lane creation is a pre-resolved-snapshot handoff: the lane conversation persists and injects exactly the execution-seeded snapshot and rendered block — no re-resolution, no Standard Agent default, no second profile injection — so a delayed lane can neither pick up a newer revision nor fail on a post-seed deletion. Lanes replay the stored block byte-identically across restarts and composer upgrades. Later library edits or deletions shall not affect the execution. Definition acceptance and workflow validate shall fail closed on dangling references, and execution start shall re-check before seeding. Global defaults and global templates shall be refused when referencing project-tier profiles; project definitions may reference all tiers.

payload.text: With an execution seeded: a lane conversation created after the referenced profile is edited and deleted still persists and injects exactly the execution-seeded snapshot (no re-resolution, no standard-agent default, single injection — proven by inspecting the lane conversation's persisted snapshot and instruction payload); two assignments of one profile with different focus produce distinct rendered blocks and hashes; an adversarial focus containing fence sequences is refused at authoring; the stored block replays byte-identically across a simulated restart; a new execution from the same definition fails closed on the deleted reference.

A global-scope defaults/template document referencing a project-tier profile is refused at save and at validate with an error naming the scope rule; a project definition referencing builtin, global, and project tiers passes.

payload.statement: A validation round shall be deterministic: (1) a persisted round/candidate identity freezes with the validator roster at round start, before any validator runs; the identity covers the candidate's tracked content (diff scope) and task-state generation — ignored build artifacts and lane logs are outside it — and the implementer cannot run while the cohort owns the candidate; (2) the script validator runs first against the frozen candidate, its outputs and logs are written outside the candidate's tracked tree, and after the script phase the engine re-verifies the candidate identity — a mismatch concludes the round as an infrastructure outcome, never a semantic verdict; (3) a deterministic script failure short-circuits the round with zero specialists launched; only after script success are the cohort specialists admitted, all concurrently, per the validator-parallelism requirement; (4) every specialist receives byte-identical common inputs — charter, invariants, acceptance criteria, task state, diff scope — differing only in its own rendered profile block; (5) remediation begins only when the round has concluded per the infrastructure requirement's rules — every specialist settled by semantic verdict or infrastructure exhaustion, or a mixed round concluded on a semantic rejection with infra-failed specialists deferred to the next round; findings stay grouped by assignment, only reopened task IDs are deduplicated, and a result arriving for a stale candidate identity is rejected, never recorded; (6) any required-validator semantic failure fails the cohort, the implementer receives all findings in one remediation pass, and the cohort charges exactly one validation iteration and one consecutive-failure count.

payload.text: Engine tests prove roster-and-candidate freeze at round start with implementer exclusion; candidate identity covering the exact reviewed tree (the temporary-index tree hash including untracked content and file modes, with gitignored artifacts and lane logs outside it) plus task-state hash; script-first execution against the frozen candidate with script outputs outside the identity; post-script identity re-verification concluding a mismatch as an infrastructure outcome with its explicit state/event/resume transition; zero specialists launched on deterministic script failure; byte-identical common inputs; and rejection of a result carrying a stale candidate identity, never recorded.

A cohort of three validators with two failures charges exactly one validation iteration and one consecutive-failure count; the circuit-breaker accounting is proven unchanged versus a single-validator failure.

payload.statement: An infrastructure failure (provider error, timeout, malformed output after structured-output repair) shall not be a review verdict: only the affected specialist retries against the unchanged frozen candidate, other specialists' collected verdicts are retained for that round, no implementation task reopens, and no validation iteration is charged. Infrastructure attempts are fixed at 3 total per specialist per round in v1 — one initial attempt plus two retries, no per-cohort configuration — with the attempt count persisted; exhaustion halts the context with an infrastructure halt kind (repairable/resumable — resuming the halt resets that round's attempt counters), and infrastructure halts are never plan-repair triggers. Mixed rounds have defined precedence: once every non-infra-failed specialist has reported, any semantic rejection concludes the round as a semantic failure (one iteration charge, remediation proceeds, the infra-failed specialists simply rerun in the next round); a round left with only infrastructure outcomes does not conclude — it remains open and uncharged with its settled verdicts retained, publishes no aggregate verdict, and specialist exhaustion halts the context resumably as above. Event semantics: the aggregate cohort validation-result event is published only for semantically concluded rounds and remains the sole evidence-ingestion record; infrastructure failures, stale-result rejections, and partial rounds publish distinct non-verdict event kinds that evidence ingestion ignores.

payload.text: Tests prove: per-specialist retry against the intact frozen candidate with other verdicts retained and no charge; the fixed bound of 3 attempts total per specialist per round (one initial plus two retries); persisted attempt counts surviving reload and resetting on halt resume; exhaustion halting with the infrastructure halt kind naming the assignment, and plan-repair not triggering on it; mixed-round precedence (semantic rejection concludes the round with one charge once reachable verdicts are in; a round left with only infrastructure outcomes stays unconcluded and uncharged — settled verdicts retained, no aggregate event — and exhaustion halts resumably); and event discipline — no aggregate verdict event for infra/stale/partial rounds, the distinct non-verdict kinds published instead, and evidence ingestion consuming only the aggregate verdict events.

payload.statement: Validator lanes shall be mechanically read-only: every validator lane, on both execution strategies and both backends, runs under a backend-enforced write-restriction envelope that makes filesystem mutation outside an explicit per-lane write allowlist impossible. The allowlist covers only a lane-scoped scratch/report directory and OS temp — never the candidate worktree. Enforcement uses each backend's native mechanism, configured at the backend-neutral capability seam: Codex via sandboxMode (read-only, or workspace-write with writable roots restricted to the allowlist); Claude via the Agent SDK sandbox (enabled, failIfUnavailable, allowUnsandboxedCommands false, filesystem write allowlist) plus permission rules/disallowedTools scoping the file-mutation tools to the same allowlist. Envelope establishment is fail-closed: a lane that cannot establish enforcement fails as an infrastructure outcome and never runs unsandboxed, and a backend that does not support the envelope is ineligible for validator assignments — refused at definition validate. The write-capable implementer configuration shall be absent from validator lanes, and a profile cannot authorize a validator to edit the candidate or approve its own fixes. The envelope governs filesystem mutation; server-mediated state remains governed by the existing choke points (live-edit surface, plan-repair allowlist) and by validator lanes not receiving implementer task tooling.

payload.text: Per-backend enforcement tests prove the envelope mechanically: a validator lane's attempted write inside the candidate worktree fails at the enforcement layer (shell writes and file-mutation tools alike) while reads succeed; writes to the lane scratch directory and OS temp succeed; sandbox-unavailable fails the lane closed as an infrastructure outcome rather than running unsandboxed; and after an adversarial validator run that attempts mutation, the candidate worktree is byte-identical to its frozen state.

Definition validate refuses a validator assignment on a backend without an enforceable envelope with a located error naming the backend and use site; the write-capable configuration used by implementer lanes (permission/sandbox mode and write-capable tool set) is proven absent from validator lanes at the backend-neutral boundary for both execution strategies.

payload.statement: The singleton context-validator lane shall generalize to per-assignment identity (context-validator:<assignment-id> or an equivalent structured key) across lane state, conversation identity, continuity, pending questions, cancellation, artifacts, reset, persistence, events, logs, and the inspector. Each assignment shall have independent continuity across semantic rounds.

payload.text: Two assignments of the same profile in one context maintain distinct lane state, continuity, artifacts, and events across two semantic rounds; cancellation acts on one assignment's in-flight turn without disturbing the other.
Every new persisted shape (assignments, cohort state, per-assignment lane records, seeded snapshots) is covered by its repository's maximal round-trip contract fixture and reloads intact from SQLite.

payload.statement: When user questions are enabled for validators, each validator lane whose transport supports asking — a conversation-strategy assignment on a backend with native mid-turn asking — may park itself on a question independently: multiple validators in one context may have questions pending simultaneously, every pending question is surfaced in the Needs You section of the conversation panel, and there is no per-context mutex and no engine-side decline — the engine never refuses an ask its transport delivers (task-strategy lanes have no ask transport and never see the tool). The human may skip an individual question; a skipped answer resumes only the asking lane, which proceeds with best judgment. A lane awaiting an answer is an unsettled outcome under the round rule: parked lanes hold the round open without blocking siblings from reviewing or asking. Completed verdicts are retained only while the candidate identity is unchanged. Editing assignments follows pause-to-edit per the live-edit requirement: pausing aborts the in-flight round and cancels all of its parked questions, and the edited roster's next round starts without residue. The default remains questions disabled.

payload.text: With two question-capable validators asking in the same round, both questions are pending simultaneously and visible as Needs You attention; the pending questions survive a server reload with both still answerable; answering one settles that lane while the sibling stays parked, and the round concludes only after both settle; near-simultaneous answers to both are each delivered to their own lane exactly once; a skipped answer resumes only the asking lane, which completes with best judgment; a verdict completed before a candidate change is discarded after it; pause-to-edit racing an incoming answer cancels all parked questions with the aborted round exactly once, and the next round runs the edited roster without residue.

payload.statement: Workflow roles shall receive composed instructions from the neutral composer through their actual transports: conversation-backed lanes via session/runtime instructions and task-strategy validation via executeWorkflowTaskRun.systemInstructions. User-authored profile text shall never be placed alone at system priority above the role contract: composition puts the role harness, scope rules, and verdict/output schema first at the authoritative layer, with the profile as a delimited subordinate lens, delivered through the strongest privileged instruction channel the backend offers for that transport (Claude's system-prompt channel; Codex developer/system instructions where available — never solely inline user-prompt text when a privileged channel exists), and permissions and output schemas enforced externally. Adversarial-profile and adversarial-focus tests on both backends shall cover scope expansion, validator editing, acceptance-criteria bypass, and verdict-schema replacement.

payload.text: Composition tests prove the role contract precedes the profile lens at the same authoritative layer and the profile block carries its subordination contract; the composed payload is asserted at the final provider invocation — the actual channel handed to the backend SDK (Claude system prompt; Codex developer/system instructions where available) — across all four backend/strategy combinations, not only at the internal transport seam.

An adversarial suite covering both adversarial profile text and adversarial assignment focus (scope expansion, candidate editing, acceptance-criteria bypass, verdict-schema replacement) passes on both backends: the verdict schema still validates, the read-only envelope holds, and scope/AC enforcement comes from the harness rather than the profile.

payload.statement: Deliberate assignment changes on a live execution (add/remove/reorder/refocus validator assignments, swap the implementer assignment; refreshing a stale snapshot is expressed as re-saving the assignment through these same ops, not a distinct operation kind) shall follow the locked D0 lifecycle: a started context is edited through pause-to-edit, pausing aborts the in-flight validation round (its collected verdicts are discarded, consistent with the rerun rule), the edit applies through the existing revisioned live-edit surface, and resume re-freezes the candidate and runs the new roster as a fresh round. Any change to an assignment's profile, focus, runtime, snapshot, execution strategy, or continuity policy shall rotate that assignment's continuity — validator and implementer lanes alike — so a stale rendered block or stale lane state is never reused; changing an assignment id is a remove-and-add, never an in-place rename. Implementer changes apply at the next implementer invocation. The plan-repair op allowlist shall exclude assignment operations.

payload.text: An assignment edit on a started context requires pause; the paused round's verdicts are discarded; resume re-freezes the candidate and runs the edited roster as a new round; continuity rotation is proven for both an edited validator assignment and an edited implementer assignment (the old rendered block is not reused after a profile/focus/runtime change); liveRevision conflict semantics hold; plan-repair attempting an assignment op is refused by the allowlist.

payload.statement: The workflow builder shall provide an implementer assignment selector and an ordered validator-cohort editor (per-assignment profile picker with tier badges, focus text, strategy, runtime) backed by the shared library picker. The execution inspector shall show, per assignment: resolved profile and revision, lane status, verdict, artifacts, and the deterministic aggregate cohort result, distinguishing semantic rejection from infrastructure failure. Event semantics preserve existing consumers per the infrastructure requirement: the aggregate cohort validation-result event (semantic rounds only) remains the record evidence ingestion and latest-verdict logic consume, and specialist-detail events carry per-assignment verdicts additively.

payload.text: Component tests cover the cohort editor on both the workflow-definition surface and the global-defaults (Settings) surface — ordering, per-assignment focus/runtime, tier badges, inherit/use/disabled cascade states, and dormant-cohort restoration on re-enable — with Storybook stories for the new component states.

The aggregate cohort validation-result event still parses for existing consumers and remains the sole evidence-ingestion record; specialist-detail events carry assignment id and profile ref/revision/hash additively; existing latest-verdict logic over the aggregate event is proven unchanged by a multi-assignment round.

payload.statement: cctl workflow validate and definition acceptance shall report assignment errors with the qualified profile reference and the exact use site (context/role/assignment id). cctl workflow surfaces (get/live get) shall display assignments with profile provenance. The graph-workflow-planning skill shall be updated to staff implementer and validator assignments from the library via cctl agent — only once the CLI contract is live.

payload.text: Validate/acceptance error contract tests prove a dangling or malformed assignment reports the qualified ref and use site; workflow get surfaces show assignment provenance; the planning-skill update lands with (not before) the live CLI contract and is confirmed by lane validator review.

payload.statement: When a cohort's failures trip the circuit breaker, the D1 plan-repair agent's evidence shall include the grouped per-assignment findings and verdicts from the final rounds; the plan-repair mutation allowlist remains unchanged (plan artifacts only, no assignment operations).

payload.text: On a breaker trip from a multi-validator cohort, the repair agent's prompt/evidence contains findings grouped by assignment with profile identity, and the allowlist test proves assignment ops remain excluded.

payload.statement: The library delete flow shall enumerate every persisted reference holder of the profile being deleted at preview: saved workflow definitions and templates in the relevant scopes — including references held by dormant assignments inside disabled cohorts — global config workflowDefaults, and, for a global-tier profile, references across all projects' definitions and templates. The enumeration is advisory: there is no acceptance-time recheck, and a reference created between preview and deletion is caught by fail-closed validation rather than by the delete flow. After deletion, affected saved artifacts fail closed at validate and launch with the located dangling-reference error — visibly unlaunchable, not silently broken — while snapshot-backed executions and conversations remain intact.

payload.text: Deleting a profile referenced by a saved definition, a template, and global workflowDefaults lists all three before confirmation; a profile referenced only by a dormant assignment inside a disabled cohort is still enumerated; a global-tier profile referenced from a second project's definition is enumerated across projects; a reference created after preview and before deletion leaves that artifact failing validate/launch with the located dangling-reference error (fail-closed, no recheck promise); after deletion each affected artifact fails validate/launch with the located error while an execution already seeded from one completes unaffected; a profile with no referencing artifacts reports none and deletes cleanly.

A real graph execution runs one context gated by at least two specialist validator assignments with distinct profiles against the same frozen candidate: both produce independent recorded verdicts, the aggregate cohort result reflects them, and the per-assignment lanes/artifacts are distinguishable in the inspector; recorded for the delivery gate.

validationStrategy.note: Live proof on a real execution; deterministic round semantics are covered by the engine tests.

payload.text: A real graph execution runs a context whose implementer assignment uses a non-default profile: the lane's persisted seeded snapshot carries that profile, the lane's behavior reflects its instructions (behavioral marker in output or transcript), and the inspector shows the implementer's profile identity; recorded for the delivery gate.

payload.text: An end-to-end run of a migrated pre-existing workflow definition proves behavioral equivalence: exactly one reviewer invocation per validation round (the migrated general assignment), unchanged iteration and circuit-breaker accounting versus the pre-migration baseline, and the migrated continuity carried across rounds; recorded for the delivery gate.

validationStrategy.note: Provable either as a live migrated run or a full-engine integration test over a migrated fixture.

payload.statement: Within a validation round, the specialist phase shall have no cohort-internal ordering: once the script validator passes against the frozen candidate, every specialist assignment is admitted for launch immediately, and no specialist's start shall wait on a sibling specialist's completion or verdict. On a deterministic script failure zero specialists launch. Actual starts are governed solely by the engine's existing global concurrency budget (maxConcurrentQueries) — the cohort introduces no additional serialization of its own. Aggregate results are assembled in configured cohort order, never completion order.

payload.text: Engine tests prove that with the global concurrency budget at or above cohort size, a cohort of at least three specialist assignments starts concurrently once the script validator passes — each specialist lane starts before any sibling verdict completes, an artificially slow specialist never delays a sibling's start, and no specialist launches before script success; with the budget below cohort size, specialists start as budget slots free with no cohort-internal ordering constraint; aggregate results assemble in configured cohort order regardless of completion order.

payload.body:
The design generalizes today's singleton roles into library-backed assignments without adding a fourth orchestration shape: everything lands inside the existing graph engine (deterministic loop, src/lib/workflow-graph/), the shared lane primitives (LaneService over graph-lane-store), the one live-edit choke point (live-edit-apply.ts), and the typed publication seam.

Configuration: a new AgentAssignment family in workflow-graph/config-schemas.ts composes the companion domain's AgentProfileRef with the existing per-backend runtime union. The implementer at every cascade tier becomes one assignment; contextValidator becomes an ordered cohort with enabled/dormant semantics and an explicit strategy field per assignment (conversation or task, independent of backend — all four backend-x-strategy combinations are legal). The resolve-config ?? chains already replace whole values per tier, so whole-unit cascade replacement needs no resolver rework; the context-tier {kind} wrapper is deleted in favor of one cohort shape at all tiers. Authored surfaces carry profile references; the execution's workingDefinition carries snapshot-bearing assignments — two schemas, one boundary.

Execution start resolves EVERY persisted assignment — implementer, enabled cohort members, and dormant assignments inside disabled cohorts alike — and stores the full 8-field snapshot (rendered by the composer's new optional assignment-focus input) on the assignment inside workingDefinition, so no later library edit or deletion can reach a running execution, including through an enable edit. Everything downstream is a pre-resolved handoff: validator turns re-send the stored block per turn through executeWorkflowTaskRun.systemInstructions — Claude delivers it via systemPrompt.append, and Codex delivers it through the live developer_instructions configuration channel (the privileged developer-role layer the isolated one-shot profile already blanks today), never inline user-prompt text — and implementer lane conversations persist the seeded snapshot verbatim through a programmatic snapshot input on conversation creation, riding the spec-A sessionInstructions channel. No re-resolution after seeding, byte-identical replay across restarts.

The engine gains its first explicit round object: a persisted validationRound on context state freezes the candidate identity — the tree hash of the same temporary git index the diff pipeline already builds (untracked content and file modes included) plus HEAD and a task-state hash — and the roster before the script phase, re-verifies it after the script phase and again before accepting any specialist result or publishing the aggregate, then admits every specialist concurrently; actual starts are governed solely by the existing global query semaphore. Specialist verdicts, infra attempts (fixed at 3, counted only after semaphore admission), and round-scoped question tokens live per assignment in the round record; conclusion applies exactly one charge and one remediation pass. Only semantically concluded rounds publish the aggregate graph-workflow-validation-result event, extended additively with ordered per-specialist entries (each carrying its own sessionRef and review artifact); kind:'output_schema' publications are untouched. Infra failures, stale results, and superseded rounds publish a distinct non-verdict incident event; today's infra-error path that publishes a fake failing verdict is deleted. A round that cannot conclude semantically because a required specialist exhausted its attempts halts resumably with its settled verdicts retained and nothing charged.

Validator lanes become per-assignment (laneStates key context_validator:<assignmentId>) with independent continuity, artifacts, questions, per-assignment reset, and events, and run mechanically read-only: a neutral filesystem write-allowlist on the task port, translated by each adapter to its OS enforcement — Codex sandboxMode workspace-write with the lane scratch directory as workspace; Claude Agent SDK sandbox with failIfUnavailable, an explicit denyWrite on the candidate worktree, trusted-only settings (no user/project/local settingSources), and a per-lane temp directory — failing closed as an infrastructure outcome. Deterministic verification that must write into the worktree stays with the engine-run script validator, which is outside the envelope by construction.

Migration is a hard cutover in the state-store runner behind the repository's schema-version barrier: config.json workflowDefaults and both tiers of scoped definition documents are rewritten in place with frozen shape-mapping rules that preserve explicit legacy values verbatim, and every pre-cutover execution row has its two JSON tiers merged into one blob, is stamped (non-terminal rows aborted with a migration-cutover reason), and moved to the archived table, whose read path gains the single approved legacy decoder and whose history actually reaches the inspector (the connected panel's archived list is wired to the real accessor). Post-cutover, the existing schema-cutover-guard refuses legacy shapes with located errors. UI (builder, runtime config tab, Settings global defaults, inspector), CLI (validate/get/live get provenance, with async project-scope-aware reference checks), evidence ingestion, and plan-repair evidence all consume the same aggregate contract; the library delete flow gains a read-only preview endpoint fed by a registered workflow reference reporter; the planning skill update lands with the live CLI contract.
payload.title: Design narrative

payload.chosenApproach: workflow-graph/config-schemas.ts gains agentAssignmentSchema { id (lowercase kebab-case, 1-64 chars, regex-enforced), profile: agentProfileRefSchema (imported from @/lib/agent-profiles/schemas — the qualified {tier,id} ref), focus?: normalized size-capped string, agent: graphWorkflowAgentConfigSchema (the existing per-backend discriminated union, concrete) } and validatorAssignmentSchema extending it with strategy: z.enum(['conversation','task']) and continuity: graphWorkflowLaneContinuityPolicySchema. validatorCohortSchema is { enabled: boolean (default true), assignments: validatorAssignment[] } with a refinement requiring at least one assignment when enabled — enabled:false with an empty list is legal (it is the honest migration of a legacy context-tier {kind:'disabled'} that carried nothing), and assignment ids must be unique within the cohort while the same profile may repeat under different focus. The implementer field at all three tiers (config.json workflowDefaults, workflowConfigOverride, context definition) becomes agentAssignmentSchema; contextValidator at all three tiers becomes the optional cohort (absent inherits, present replaces the whole set, enabled:false preserves dormant assignments); the context-tier contextValidatorOverrideSchema {kind:'use'|'disabled'} wrapper is deleted. The resolve-config.ts ?? chains already select whole values per tier, so whole-unit replacement holds without resolver rework; resolveGraphWorkflowValidatorExecutionPlan and the provider-named type discriminator are deleted — dispatch reads assignment.strategy directly, making all four backend-x-strategy combinations expressible (a Codex agent under conversation strategy is already legal today; Claude under task strategy becomes legal). SEEDED_WORKFLOW_DEFAULTS seeds implementer as { id:'implementer', profile: builtin:general-implementer, agent: claude/opus/medium } and contextValidator as a cohort of exactly one { id:'general', profile: builtin:general-reviewer, strategy:'conversation', agent: claude/sonnet/medium, continuity:{enabled:true} } — single-sourced, preserving today's one-reviewer cost profile. computeUsedBackends collects the implementer assignment's backend plus every enabled cohort assignment's backend.
payload.reason: One schema family, owned where the cascade lives, makes whole-unit replacement, dormant retention, and strategy/backend independence structural instead of conventional.

rejectedAlternatives.label: Keep the {kind:'use'|'disabled'} context wrapper and add a parallel cohort field
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Two validator encodings at different tiers is exactly the asymmetry that made today's disabled state lossy; the wrapper cannot carry dormant assignments, which R2 requires.

rejectedAlternatives.label: Field-level merge of assignments across tiers
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Locked out by Alex (2026-08-01): assignments replace whole at each override boundary; merging reintroduces the cross-tier provenance ambiguity the collaboration-config resolver needed special machinery to track.

rejectedAlternatives.label: Keep strategy encoded in a provider-named discriminator (today's type field)
rejectedAlternatives.reason: type:'codex' conflates strategy with backend, making Claude-task and future backend-strategy combinations inexpressible and forcing the translation shim the seam steering says to avoid.

payload.title: AgentAssignment + ordered cohort schemas replace the singleton roles at every cascade tier

payload.chosenApproach: A new state-store runner migration (src/lib/state-store/migrations/, registered in index.ts, using MigrationContext.configDir) converts the three persisted surfaces with mapping rules frozen inside the migration file (no live schema/resolver imports, per the 0008/0009 lesson). It is a BREAKING migration and follows the 0005/0009 protocol exactly: publishSchemaCompatibilityBarrier(configDir, N) before the transaction, KNOWN_SCHEMA_VERSION bumped, enforceCurrentSchemaCompatibility witnessed inside the write lock, and the schema_migrations row inserted in the same transaction. Surfaces: (1) config.json workflowDefaults — read the raw file directly (not readRawConfig, which silently degrades to {} on parse failure) and rewrite via atomicWriteJson, since loader writes are non-atomic; (2) every scoped definition document under <configDir>/workflows/<scopeKey>/*.json in both tiers; (3) every graph_workflow_executions row: merge its two persisted JSON tiers (definition_json + runtime_json) into one execution blob with a frozen copy of the repository's shallow tier merge — inventing no fields and no snapshot provenance — compute cutover-terminality from a frozen copy of the status/halt taxonomy (terminal = completed, aborted, or halted with a non-resumable reason; the codebase has no 'failed' execution status), stamp every non-terminal row status:'aborted' with an additive halt-reason payload on the {type:'aborted'} variant (cause:'migration_cutover' plus a human summary, following the max_iterations.summary precedent; HALT_RESUMABILITY keeps aborted:false), then INSERT the raw blob into graph_workflow_archived_executions via raw SQL and empty the active table. Value preservation rule: explicitly persisted legacy values — including Codex model/effort strings — are copied verbatim, never re-derived, clamped, or narrowed against any enum (the migration transforms shape, not values; load-time validation governs values exactly as it does today); only ABSENT optional fields materialize, through a frozen copy of the effective-value chain (config.json agentBackends profile -> the current descriptor default, with the model-aware effort clamp). Legacy shape mapping: implementer triple -> assignment id:'implementer' on builtin:general-implementer; contextValidator -> cohort of one id:'general' on builtin:general-reviewer with strategy from the legacy type (claude->conversation, codex->task) and continuity carried over; validator enabled:false -> cohort {enabled:false} carrying the dormant assignment; context {kind:'disabled'} -> cohort {enabled:false, assignments:[]}. Idempotence predicate: a document already in assignment shape never re-matches; the emptied active table makes the row phase a natural no-op on replay; the DB phase runs in one transaction(...).immediate() and file rewrites are individually atomic, so a crash between them resumes without double-applying (failure-injection tests per R3.1). Post-cutover refusal extends the existing schema-cutover-guard.ts (assertNoLegacyWorkflowFields / LegacyWorkflowSchemaError) and plan-validation.ts to refuse legacy keys with a located error naming the use site and expected assignment form. The single approved back-compat exception lands in graph-workflow-archived-executions-repo.findByExecution: a frozen read-only legacy decoder tried when current-schema parse fails, never writing back; listArchived gains per-row skip-with-diagnostic so one legacy blob cannot fail the whole history list. Visibility is real, not asserted: the connected workflow panel currently hardcodes archivedExecutions=[] (ConnectedGraphWorkflowPanel.tsx:288), so this spec wires the existing archived-summaries accessor through a query into the panel and renders the migration-cutover abort reason on archived entries — that is where 'surfaced in the inspector' is discharged.
payload.reason: Emptying the active table at cutover behind the established version barrier is what makes 'no inbound compat parser' literally true, and verbatim value copy keeps the migration a shape transform with zero semantic authority.

rejectedAlternatives.label: Upgrade non-terminal executions in place (rekey lanes, carry continuity and pending questions)
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Rejected by Alex (2026-08-03): live-runtime migration was dropped wholesale — lane rekeys, continuity records, and pending questions do not carry across the cutover; abort-with-reason is the whole contract.

rejectedAlternatives.label: Leave terminal rows in the active table and teach the active read path both shapes
rejectedAlternatives.reason: That is an inbound compatibility parser on the live path — locked out. Archiving every pre-cutover row confines legacy decoding to the one approved floor and leaves the active table uniformly new-shape.

rejectedAlternatives.label: Re-derive or enum-clamp explicit legacy model/effort values during migration
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Silently rewriting an explicitly configured value falsifies the operator's record; shape mapping with verbatim value copy keeps the migration honest and leaves value validation where it lives today — at load time.

rejectedAlternatives.label: Rewrite archived blobs to the new shape
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Archives are immutable history; rewriting them is risk without benefit (Alex approved the read-path floor on exactly this reasoning, spec question Q1).

payload.title: One runner migration behind the schema barrier: merge, stamp, and archive every pre-cutover execution; rewrite config surfaces in place; decode floor on the archived read path only

payload.chosenApproach: The companion composer gains the one focus-aware interface this spec adds: composeProfileBlock(profile, options?: { assignmentFocus?: string }) and buildAgentProfileSnapshot(profile, options?) in src/lib/agent-profiles/composer.ts. Focus is trimmed/NFC-normalized, size-capped by a shared constant, refused at authoring when it contains the composer's reserved sequences (findReservedSequence — the same delimiter/fence rules as profile content), rendered exactly once as a dedicated sub-section inside the delimited block, and therefore covered by resolvedInstructionHash; focus is never delivered through any second channel. Two schema shapes with one boundary: authored surfaces (definitions, templates, workflowDefaults) carry reference-bearing assignments; the execution's workingDefinition carries snapshot-bearing assignments. At execution start, after cascade resolution, the seed path resolves EVERY persisted assignment through the library service — the implementer, every enabled cohort member, and every dormant assignment inside a disabled cohort — and stores the full snapshot { tier, id, name, revision, sourceContentHash, instructions, renderedInstructionBlock, resolvedInstructionHash } on each (bounded by cohort size for the blob-bounds registry). Enabling a dormant assignment mid-run therefore uses its execution-seeded snapshot with no library access, so profile edits or deletions after start cannot reach the execution through ANY path, including an enable edit — R4's immutability holds unconditionally. Definition acceptance (storage.ts accept-time validation) and cctl workflow validate fail closed on dangling refs; execution start re-resolves before seeding so a post-validate deletion still fails closed. Scope rule: global-scope documents (global templates, config.json workflowDefaults) are refused at save and at validate when any assignment references a project-tier profile; project definitions may reference all tiers. Lane creation consumes only the seeded snapshot: validator turns send the stored renderedInstructionBlock per turn (see the transport decision), and implementer lane conversations pass the execution-seeded snapshot verbatim through a new programmatic snapshot input on conversation creation — the conversation persists it as its profileSnapshot and injects the stored block, with no library re-resolution, no Standard Agent default, and no second injection. A lane created after the profile is edited or deleted still runs the seeded bytes; replay after restart re-sends the stored block byte-identically.
payload.reason: Seeding the full rendered snapshot for every persisted assignment once, then treating every downstream consumer as a dumb replayer, is the only shape in which R4's immunity claim is unconditional.

rejectedAlternatives.label: Snapshot only enabled assignments and re-resolve dormant ones when a live edit enables them
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Review finding (2026-08-03): re-resolution at enable time lets a post-seed profile edit or deletion alter a running execution — a direct contradiction of R4's 'later library edits or deletions shall not affect the execution'.

rejectedAlternatives.label: Store only the profile ref at seed time and resolve at lane creation
rejectedAlternatives.reason: A delayed lane could pick up a newer revision or fail on a deleted profile — exactly the drift/fragility R4 forbids; the execution must own its bytes from the moment it starts.

rejectedAlternatives.label: Deliver focus as a separate prompt section outside the rendered block
rejectedAlternatives.reason: A second channel would escape resolvedInstructionHash coverage and the block's subordination contract — the hash must attest to every profile-derived byte the model sees.

payload.title: Execution start snapshots EVERY persisted assignment — dormant included; every lane is a pre-resolved handoff

payload.chosenApproach: Context state gains validationRound (runtime tier, nullable): { seq (monotonic per context), candidate: { headSha, candidateTreeHash, taskStateHash }, roster: [{ assignmentId, profileRef, revision, resolvedInstructionHash, strategy }], specialists: per-assignment { state: pending|running|verdict_pass|verdict_fail|infra_failed|parked, attempts, summary?, issues?, questionToken? }, phase, startedAt } — bounded by cohort size. The round freezes at round start, before any validator runs. Candidate identity covers exactly what validators review: candidateTreeHash is the git tree hash written from the same TEMPORARY INDEX the diff pipeline already builds (src/lib/git/diff.ts stages untracked files into a temp index precisely so they appear in the rendered diff), so untracked content and file-mode changes are inside the identity, while gitignored build artifacts and lane logs remain outside it; headSha pins the base and taskStateHash covers the context's task tuples. The implementer cannot run while the round is open: the engine's existing within-context serialization already guarantees it, and the seed path adds an explicit refusal while validationRound is non-null as a structural guard. The script validator keeps its existing script-first position (processContextCompletionValidation runs processScriptValidation before any agent validation) and its existing worktree log location (.cc/workflow/ is gitignored, hence outside the identity — pinned by test); a deterministic script failure short-circuits with zero specialists launched and keeps its existing remediation-task accounting. The engine recomputes the candidate identity at three points: after the script phase (a mismatch concludes the round as an infrastructure outcome — non-verdict event, no charge, no specialists), before accepting each specialist result (a result carrying a stale (seq, candidate) pair is rejected as an incident, never recorded), and before publishing the aggregate result. On script success every specialist is dispatched simultaneously (Promise.all over per-assignment lanes); each receives byte-identical common inputs — the common prompt sections (charter, invariants, acceptance criteria, task state, diff scope) are rendered once per round and shared, with only the assignment's own rendered profile block differing. Conclusion follows the infra decision's rules; on a semantic failure the engine applies ONE consecutiveFailureCount increment and one reopen mutation for the whole round (findings grouped by assignment, only reopened task IDs deduplicated across specialists), and a pass resets the counter exactly as today, so circuit-breaker accounting is provably unchanged versus a single validator.
payload.reason: Hashing the exact temporary-index tree makes the freeze claim coextensive with what specialists actually see, and the persisted round object is what turns determinism (same candidate, same roster, one charge) into an enforceable predicate.

rejectedAlternatives.label: Hash only the tracked-file diff for candidate identity
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Review finding (2026-08-03): validators receive untracked files through the temporary git index, and a parsed-diff hash can also miss mode changes — the identity must cover the exact tree under review, or an untracked-file mutation slips past the freeze.

rejectedAlternatives.label: Derive rounds implicitly from the event log (today's shape) instead of a persisted record
rejectedAlternatives.reason: There is no round identity today — stale-result rejection, per-specialist attempts, and reload-surviving parked lanes all need a durable object; an implicit round cannot refuse a stale verdict.

rejectedAlternatives.label: Freeze the candidate by committing it (temporary commit or stash) at round start
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Mutating git state to observe it perturbs the working tree the implementer resumes on; write-tree over the already-built temp index is observation without mutation.

payload.title: A persisted validationRound freezes the exact reviewed tree and roster; specialists run concurrently against it

payload.chosenApproach: Infrastructure outcomes (provider error, timeout, post-repair malformed output — today's infra_error reasons) never become verdicts: only the affected specialist retries against the unchanged frozen candidate, sibling verdicts already recorded in the round stand, no task reopens, and no iteration or failure count is charged. Attempts are fixed at 3 total per specialist per round (one initial plus two retries, a constant — no per-cohort configuration), persisted in the round record so they survive reload, and counted only for dispatches that were actually admitted: a global-semaphore admission timeout is queue pressure, not a specialist failure, and does not consume an attempt. Round conclusion is a single precedence rule with no ambiguity: (a) once every non-infra-failed specialist has reported, any semantic rejection concludes the round as a semantic failure — one charge, one remediation pass, and the infra-failed specialists simply run again in the next round; (b) all specialists passing concludes the round as a pass; (c) a round with no semantic rejection where a required specialist has exhausted its attempts CANNOT conclude — all-of semantics make an unheard required validator an unconcludable round — so it halts the context with the existing validator_infra_error halt kind extended additively { assignmentId, attempts, roundSeq }, the round record and its settled verdicts RETAINED, nothing charged, and no aggregate event published. HALT_RESUMABILITY keeps the kind resumable; resuming resets the round's attempt counters, re-verifies the candidate identity, and reruns only the unsettled specialists. The plan-repair trigger (workflow-graph/plan-repair/trigger.ts) continues to fire only on circuit_breaker and max_iterations — infrastructure halts are never plan-repair triggers, pinned by test. Event discipline: the aggregate graph-workflow-validation-result is published only for semantically concluded rounds and remains the sole evidence-ingestion record; a new graph-workflow-validator-incident event kind { incident: infra_failure | infra_exhausted | stale_result_rejected | round_superseded, assignmentId?, roundSeq } covers everything non-verdict, and evidence ingestion ignores it by its existing event-type filter. Today's path that publishes a pass:false aggregate event for an infra error (iteration-orchestrator.ts:1383-1395) is deleted.
payload.reason: Verdicts must mean 'the review concluded'; an unheard required validator means the round cannot conclude — encoding that as a retained, resumable, uncharged halt removes the last ambiguity between operational noise and review outcomes.

rejectedAlternatives.label: Conclude an infra-only round as an uncharged non-result instead of halting
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Review finding (2026-08-03): 'concluded uncharged' and 'halted' were both stated in rev 8 — ambiguous. Retained-and-halted is the correct reading of R6: a required validator was never heard, so the round must not conclude; the halt preserves settled verdicts and resume reruns only the gap.

rejectedAlternatives.label: Configurable retry budget per cohort or per assignment
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Locked at 3 total in requirements review — configuration here is speculative surface area with real cascade/migration cost and no demonstrated need.

rejectedAlternatives.label: Keep publishing an aggregate failing verdict on infra errors (today's behavior)
rejectedAlternatives.reason: An infra failure masquerading as a review verdict charges iterations, poisons latest-verdict feedback, and can trip the breaker on flaky providers — the precise defect R6 removes.

rejectedAlternatives.label: Count semaphore-admission timeouts as attempts
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Queue pressure under a busy budget would burn a specialist's retry budget without the specialist ever running — exhaustion must measure provider failures, not scheduling load.

payload.title: Fixed 3 post-admission attempts per specialist; exhaustion halts resumably with verdicts retained; incidents are never verdicts

payload.chosenApproach: The write policy is SERVER-DERIVED and travels the entire task transport so no intermediate layer can drop it: ExecuteWorkflowTaskRunInput gains fsWritePolicy?: { mode: 'allowlist', allowWrite: string[], denyWrite: string[] } (absent = today's unrestricted behavior), carried through the SUBMIT_TASK_RUN machine event, the actor task-run input, the neutral AgentCallRequest, the facade's task resolution, and dispatchTaskRun onto AgentTaskRequest — with the descriptor task facet declaring fsWriteRestriction: 'enforced' | 'unsupported' and a backend proven unable to enforce marked unsupported rather than enforced. Validator dispatch always passes allowWrite [laneScratchDir, laneTmpDir] and denyWrite [candidate worktree]; all policy paths are realpath-normalized at composition (macOS /tmp -> /private/tmp; symlinked worktrees) so enforcement compares canonical paths. Codex translation: sandboxMode 'workspace-write' with workingDirectory = lane scratch dir, TMPDIR = laneTmpDir, and a HERMETIC config profile for validator runs modeled on the isolated one-shot baseConfig — explicit config overrides neutralizing inherited user config, extra writable roots (sandbox_workspace_write.writable_roots set to exactly the policy), ambient temp exclusions, and non-CC-managed MCP servers — so nothing outside CC's composition widens the sandbox. Claude translation: Options.sandbox { enabled: true, failIfUnavailable: true, allowUnsandboxedCommands: false, filesystem: { allowWrite: [scratch, laneTmp], denyWrite: [worktreePath] } } (explicit deny because allowWrite is additive), settingSources: [] (no user/project/local settings — a settings file committed into the candidate must not widen its reviewer's permissions), permissionMode bypass REMOVED, and path-scoped permission rules for the file-mutation tools (Edit/Write/NotebookEdit rule content pinned to the allowlist) with unmatched requests denied — tool exclusion alone cannot express scratch-only paths, so rules + sandbox filesystem enforce it together. Envelope establishment is fail-closed: a lane that cannot establish enforcement fails as an infrastructure outcome and never runs unsandboxed. Definition validate refuses validator assignments on backends without fsWriteRestriction:'enforced'. The write-capable implementer configuration (danger-full-access / bypassPermissions literals at the single dispatch site) becomes lane-role-derived and is proven absent from validator dispatch at the neutral boundary for both strategies. Enforcement proof includes adversarial tests against the REAL installed runners on both backends (shell writes and file-mutation tools inside the worktree fail; scratch/lane-temp writes succeed; worktree byte-identical after), not only injected-deps seams. Deterministic verification that must write into the worktree stays with the engine-run script validator, outside any lane envelope by construction.
payload.reason: The envelope is only mechanical if the policy is server-derived end to end, the backend config is hermetic, paths are canonical, and the proof runs against the real runners — anything less is a convention wearing a sandbox costume.

rejectedAlternatives.label: Policy composed only at the dispatch site without transport plumbing (rev 10 shape)
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Plan review (2026-08-03): no trusted filesystem policy travels the task-run event/state/actor chain today — without end-to-end plumbing the adapter cannot distinguish a validator run from the hardcoded write-capable default, and the guarantee is not decision-complete.

rejectedAlternatives.label: Inherited backend config (user settings, ambient MCPs, default writable roots) under the sandbox
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Inherited configuration is an unaudited widening channel; the hermetic profile already exists for isolated one-shots and is the proven shape for CC-composed-only policy.

rejectedAlternatives.label: Detect-restore-and-bound
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Superseded by Alex (2026-08-03): mechanical prevention replaces detection.

rejectedAlternatives.label: Prompt-level prohibition plus post-turn git-status verification
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Prompt rules are advice to an adversary; R7 requires impossibility at the enforcement layer.

payload.title: Server-derived write-allowlist through the full task transport, hermetic backend translation, fail-closed

payload.chosenApproach: The laneStates inner record key generalizes from the bare lane kind to a lane key: 'implementer' | 'context_validator:<assignmentId>'. The lane record (graphWorkflowAgentSessionStateSchema) gains assignmentId and an assignment fingerprint (profile resolvedInstructionHash + strategy + continuity policy + runtime triple) used by rotation; graphLaneId gains the assignment as a third NUL-joined segment with parseGraphLaneId widened accordingly, so LaneService/graph-lane-store give every assignment an independent durable lane with no primitive-layer changes. The synthetic task-strategy conversation id gains the assignment segment. Each assignment has independent continuity across semantic rounds, independent pending questions (see the question decision), per-assignment artifacts (validator prompt/response/log files live under the per-assignment scratch dir from the envelope decision), and per-assignment event identity — the validation event sessionRef gains an additive assignmentId field. Cancellation acts per assignment: aborting a round cancels exactly the specialists' in-flight turns via the existing conversation abort registry, and removing/editing one assignment retires only its lane conversation and continuity. R8.1's per-assignment reset is satisfied directly: resetting one assignment (exposed on the inspector's per-assignment view, legal while the execution is paused/halted like today's whole-context reset) retires that lane conversation, deletes that laneStates entry, clears that assignment's round entry, and forces rotation on its next round — the same primitives the remove-and-add path already composes — without touching sibling lanes. Whole-context reset keeps its existing semantics (drops all lanes). collectLaneConversationIds iterates the widened key space unchanged, so pause/abort/halt/resume cancellation keeps working. Every new persisted shape — assignments in resolved contexts, snapshots, validationRound, widened laneStates keys, per-lane pending questions — lands in the executions repository's maximal round-trip contract fixture, with the split-symmetry test forcing tier assignment for any new top-level field.
payload.reason: Extending the existing composite key preserves every durable-lane guarantee while making assignments first-class exactly where state, cancellation, reset, and provenance must distinguish them.

rejectedAlternatives.label: Whole-context reset only (narrow R8.1 to match)
rejectedAlternatives.reason: R8.1 is an approved criterion ('cancellation and reset act on one assignment without disturbing the other') and per-assignment reset falls out of the retire+drop+rotate primitives this design already builds for remove-and-add — honoring the requirement is cheaper than amending it.

rejectedAlternatives.label: Widen the lane-kind enum with per-assignment members
rejectedAlternatives.reason: The enum is closed vocabulary shared with events and UI; assignment ids are open user data and belong in a structured key plus an explicit field, not in enum space.

rejectedAlternatives.label: A separate per-assignment lane table outside the execution row
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Lane state is execution-lifetime and already versioned/fenced through mutateActive on the execution row; a second store would need its own fencing and cleanup for no query benefit.

payload.title: Per-assignment lane keys with per-assignment reset, across state, continuity, artifacts, and events

payload.chosenApproach: The context-state field pendingUserInput becomes pendingUserInputs: a record keyed by lane key, each entry the existing parked-batch shape plus a round-scoped token { roundSeq, questionBatchId }. Clean post-cutover schema change (pre-cutover rows are archived). Question capability is transport-honest per the amended R9: conversation-strategy assignments on backends declaring nativeMidTurnAskUser (the existing predicate generalized per assignment); task-strategy lanes never see the tool. Gate verbs take a laneKey: enterAwaitingUserInput writes its own lane's slot (multiple validators park simultaneously; no per-context mutex, no engine-side decline); the existing FAST-ANSWER path is preserved exactly — recordAnswers may upsert-before-park for the asking lane's in-flight batch, and enterAwaitingUserInput finding those answers returns 'answers_ready' so the lane proceeds without parking; token checking rejects only genuinely stale submissions (a batch matching neither an actively parked entry's token nor the asking lane's current in-flight ask — withdrawn, superseded, or re-asked questions refuse with the existing 410 semantics). consumeAnswers resumes only the asking lane; a skipped answer resumes that lane with best judgment. A parked specialist is state 'parked' in the round record — an unsettled outcome holding the round open while siblings continue reviewing, verdicting, or asking; a reload with one lane parked and a sibling mid-review restores BOTH independently (the parked lane never serializes the cohort). Completed verdicts are retained only while the candidate identity is unchanged; the context stays awaiting_user_input while any lane is parked and the completion guard keeps refusing. Pause clears the round and withdraws exactly the round's parked validator questions (CLEAR_PENDING_QUESTION + resolved(withdrawn), exactly once, serialized in the write queue — a racing answer lands before the withdrawal or is refused by its dead token) while an implementer parked question survives pause as today. Abort withdraws everything. Parked records live in the runtime tier and survive reload answerable.
payload.reason: Token-checked per-lane parking that preserves the fast-answer window resolves concurrency, skips, pause races, and reloads by identity comparison while changing none of the gate's proven ergonomics.

rejectedAlternatives.label: Strict actively-parked-only answer acceptance (rev 10 wording)
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Plan review (2026-08-03): the gate's upsert-before-park fast-answer path is deliberate production behavior — rejecting answers that arrive before the park lands would regress it; the token must reject stale submissions, not fast ones.

rejectedAlternatives.label: Per-context question mutex
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Superseded by Alex (2026-08-03): serializing questions across a concurrent cohort couples independent lanes.

rejectedAlternatives.label: Build an ask transport for task-strategy lanes
rejectedAlternatives.reason: New backend machinery this spec does not need; the amended R9 scopes asking to transports that support it.

payload.title: Per-lane parked questions with round-scoped tokens; fast answers preserved; parked lanes never serialize siblings

payload.chosenApproach: Composition order is owned above the adapters: for every workflow role the authoritative instruction payload is [role harness + scope rules + verdict/output schema contract] first, then the assignment's rendered profile block (which already carries its subordination contract text from the spec-A composer) — user-authored profile text is never placed alone at system priority above the role contract. Validator lanes on BOTH strategies receive this payload per turn through executeWorkflowTaskRun.systemInstructions: the Claude task runner delivers it via the SDK's privileged systemPrompt { preset: claude_code, append } channel; the Codex task runner delivers it through the CLI's live developer_instructions configuration channel — a per-run CodexOptions.config override emitted at the developer role above user input, proven available in the installed integration by the isolated one-shot profile already blanking exactly this key (codex/task-runner.ts:485) — for new AND resumed turns alike, and the fenced '## System Instructions' user-prompt block is DROPPED for validator task runs (never solely inline user-prompt text when a privileged channel exists, per R10).
